newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy defence minister backs women in army.
newsitem.headline: Italy defence minister backs women in army.

text.p: Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta has given his backing to proposals that women be allowed to serve voluntarily in the armed forces.
Andreatta's proposal, issued on Tuesday in a speech to the parliamentary defence commission, eventually will have to go before the legislature in order to become law.
Andreatta said it should be up to parliament, the armed forces and a parliamentary commission on equal opportunities to agree on which positions Italian women could hold in the armed forces.
Italy's armed forces are currently made up of male conscripts who serve for a year or more and men who make a career of the military.
Women's groups, some members of parliament and the parliamentary commission on equal opportunities have for years proposed that women be allowed to serve in the armed forces.

Anna Finocchiaro, chairwoman of the parliamentary equal opportunities commission, said that if women are allowed to join the armed forces they should be able to hold all positions held by men, including chiefs of staff.
